item.title: Naples Pier Reef Deployment: Hurricane Ian debris becomes artificial reef; rebuilding project continues
item.description: In an inspiring move, pieces from the historical Naples Pier, damaged by Hurricane Ian, are being transformed into vital marine habitats. This initiative involves placing 59 concrete pilings at Wasmer Reef, providing support for diverse marine life. Not only does this project recycle construction debris, but it also fosters new ecosystems. Future reconstruction efforts for Naples Pier will emphasize improved safety and resilience to withstand upcoming storms.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Could the dodo return? US firm maps 95% of its genome and identifies gene-editing targets
item.description: Colossal Biosciences aims to resurrect the extinct dodo bird using cutting-edge gene-editing technologies. By leveraging their sophisticated AI platform, GenoMorph, the company has pinpointed essential genetic traits. With 95% of the dodo genome analysis complete, their ambitious project is on track, though a specific timeline for the living dodo remains undisclosed. This groundbreaking venture is part of a larger initiative to counteract the effects of human-induced species extinction.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Sara Blakely invested $5,000 in Spanx while selling fax machines; 21 years later, it is worth $1.2bn
item.description: Sara Blakely founded Spanx in 2000 with $5,000 in savings while working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson. Despite having no formal business training or outside investment, she built the company into a global womenswear brand. In 2021, Blackstone acquired a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation, with Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joining as investors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Archaeologists find 19 injuries in 12 people buried in Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia
item.description: Archaeologists found evidence of traumatic injuries in 12 individuals from Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia. These injuries were discovered in domestic spaces like houses, pits, and wells across various sites. Examination of the remains revealed sharp-force and blunt-force injuries indicating potential violence in their lives. Researchers proposed that social conditions may have contributed to the unusual burial practices observed.

item.title: Montana rancher’s rare Nanotyrannus fossil goes on display ahead of $9M auction
item.description: A rare find in the form of a nearly 70 percent complete Nanotyrannus skeleton, affectionately named Jodi, has been unearthed by rancher Jodi Pierson in Montana and is set to go under the hammer at Sotheby’s in New York on October 27. This well-preserved specimen is anticipated to garner between $6 million and $9 million, creating a buzz among paleontologists and collectors alike due to its invaluable significance.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Once the fastest US liner, SS United States is set to become the world’s largest artificial reef
item.description: The historic ocean liner SS United States is set to be intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida, transforming it into the largest artificial reef in the world. This initiative follows successful environmental remediation and requires final approvals. To honor its legacy, a visitor center will be established, promoting tourism and attracting divers and anglers eager to explore this underwater attraction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tech Aids Lost Birdsong Recovery: Synthetic calls help sparrows relearn old songs; scientists weigh AI’s role
item.description: A groundbreaking approach has emerged, leveraging computer-generated recordings to rejuvenate the bird songs that nature has lost. Researchers successfully reintroduced the unique call of the rufous-collared sparrow back into its habitat in Argentina. This innovative conservation strategy seeks to bolster endangered species by preserving their vocal heritage and fostering communication skills, as demonstrated by positive outcomes in captive breeding for species such as the regent honeyeater.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 'Go to jail or be shot’: Trump warns US military secret leakers
item.description: Trump issued a warning to those leaking military secrets, suggesting jail or execution as consequences. He also discussed the bombing of Iran's nuclear facilities and threats against leakers. The Pentagon is planning a live-stream execution of Nidal Malik Hasan for his 2009 attack at Fort Hood. Trump confirmed support for this execution, emphasizing that he is indifferent to the method used.

item.title: Con Edison’s $300M Bronx substation mimics a row of homes as $47.3M upgrade gets approval
item.description: Con Edison is set to invest $47.3 million in enhancing the East 179th Street substation in the Bronx. This vital upgrade will include the installation of a fifth transformer and a new feeder line. The initiative aims to bolster the local electric capacity, facilitating support for electrification and electric vehicles.

item.title: NYC subway hides ventilation shaft and emergency exit behind 1847 Brooklyn townhouse façade
item.description: Nestled at 58 Joralemon Street in Brooklyn Heights lies a historic brownstone that harbors a subway ventilation shaft beneath its surface. Established in 1847, it transformed into a vital transit hub in 1908 under the Brooklyn Rapid Transit Company. The building's unchanged facade allows it to integrate seamlessly into the neighborhood while fulfilling crucial safety roles.

item.title: Lake Ringgold Reservoir Permit: Judge overturns state approval; Wichita Falls weighs appeal
item.description: In a significant legal development, a Texas judge has scrapped the permit for the Lake Ringgold reservoir, amidst ongoing opposition from local ranchers concerned about environmental issues and property rights. Wichita Falls aims to appeal this ruling as they push for their water supply plans. This situation underscores the complex relationship between infrastructure advancements and conservation, with the city's next moves remaining unclear.

item.title: Walsh Warns On AI Chatbots: US commentator fears ‘friend-like’ bonds; questions big tech power
item.description: Matt Walsh criticized the growing use of AI chatbots among young people in an October 14 post on X. He warned that people could begin treating AI systems as friends and spending much of their day talking to them. Walsh has also raised concerns about AI's effects on jobs, films, music, and advertising, arguing that technology could change human relationships and creative work.

item.title: In 1930, a Pittsburgh plumber built an aluminium observatory that helped him meet Einstein
item.description: Established in 1930 by Leo Scanlon, the Valley View Observatory in Pittsburgh quickly gained traction among amateur astronomers, primarily due to its cost-effective construction and unique aluminium dome. Scanlon's fresh approach drew attention from enthusiasts nationwide, leading to a memorable encounter with Albert Einstein in 1934, who appreciated the spirit of amateur science. To honor its significant role in astronomy, asteroid 8131 was named 'Scanlon', recognizing the observatory's legacy.

item.title: Georgia farmer turned scrap metal into folk art, filling his yard with figures that reached museums
item.description: After stepping away from farming and preaching, Reuben Aaron Miller channeled his creativity into art. He crafted enchanting, wind-powered whirligigs and striking metal figures that captured the attention of collectors near and far. His partnership with R.E.M. propelled his art to new heights, significantly boosting its market value. Now featured in numerous museum exhibitions, Miller's work continues to resonate within the American folk-art community.
